confidence_reason: Current source plus focused built-browser normal, safe recovery, and fatal recovery routes establish mechanics; human discovery remains unobserved.

confirmed: Two ferries, short DNA bridge, STOP, STEADY, RESCUE, boomerang, and slime gaps are real.
Distinct hero roles and multiple transitions are necessary in the demonstrated both-exit route.
missed_mechanics: STEADY brakes the far ferry as well as stabilizing the bridge; Pac deliberately releases it only after Isp boards.
RESCUE permanently supports Pac's follow-up, and an unsupported bridge wait can kill.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass treated a far STOP platform as a separate control; the far ferry is braked by Pac's STEADY pad, while the apparent STOP marking is ferry state text.
The first pass suggested narrow chained timing with few safe pauses; focused rehold and missed-boarding routes prove local safe retries.
changed_judgments: Cooperation rises from 3 to 4 because STEADY requires a coordinated hold-and-release with Isp aboard, beyond sequential handoffs.
Timing falls from 3 to 2 because the far ferry can be arrested again and failed boarding can be retried safely.
Recovery changes from unknown to 2 because local retries exist but bridge death restarts the room.
Clarity falls as burden from 3 to 2 because visible ferry state and pad response help explain the brake, although discovery is unmeasured.
unresolved: Whether two new humans notice STEADY's second effect, and how they manage simultaneous keys, remains unknown.

single_operator_note: One person must maintain Pac's STEADY while steering Isp onto the second ferry, then release Pac at the right moment. This extra divided-attention demand is outside the two-human baseline.
